issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Ride attribute 'abbreviation' as type char (problem_statement.md), but the solution implements Ride.abbreviation as a String (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java). This discrepancy between the specified UML attribute type and the implemented type will confuse students about the correct attribute type to use and the expected constructor/getter signatures.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of 'abbreviation' consistent with the UML: change Ride.abbreviation to char (private char abbreviation), update the Ride constructor to accept a char abbreviation, and change getAbbreviation() to return char. Ensure all subclasses and usages are updated accordingly (or, alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to specify String if that was intended).

issues.description: The solution's RollerCoaster constructor declares parameter 'char abbreviation' while the solution's Ride constructor expects a String abbreviation. Passing the char abbreviation to super(name, abbreviation) causes a type mismatch and will not compile. This also conflicts with the UML requirement that subclass constructors must accept superclass attributes first: the expected types must match the superclass definition.
issues.suggestedFix: Align constructor parameter types between superclass and subclass. Preferably update Ride to use char for abbreviation (so Ride(String name, char abbreviation)) to match RollerCoaster and the UML. Alternatively, change RollerCoaster to accept a String abbreviation if the intended design uses String; then update all subclasses accordingly. Ensure the subclass constructors call super(...) with matching parameter types.
